subject: history
title: Revolution, Napoleon & the settlement of 1815
objective: A first circuit completed, not history finished

lesson.opening: Which institutions survived revolutionary and military upheaval, and which were remade?

sections.heading: The institutional thread
sections.body:
Fiscal crisis, representation, and sovereignty

War, revolution, and administrative change

Napoleonic government and the Vienna settlement

sections.heading: A model to test
sections.body: Do not substitute an inevitable march toward a predetermined future for explanation. Compare stages, actors, constraints, and consequences. Use the end of this pass to choose a region or problem for deeper study.

activities.prompt: Which happened first: “French Revolution begins” or “Waterloo and Vienna settlement”?
activities.hint: Compare the dates on the unit timeline.

activities.prompt: “Napoleon’s rise was an inevitable consequence of the events of 1789.” — is that an event claim or an interpretation?
activities.hint: Inevitability is a claim about alternatives and causation. Sequence alone cannot establish it.
